entityDescription:
The Copernicus Science Centre is one of the largest science centres in Europe. Its exhibition is divided into six interdisciplinary parts with over 450 exhibits. Music is combined here with biology, and mathematics with architecture. Science enters the realm of feelings, and the visitors themselves may become the object of observation.

The variety of exhibits gathered at several thousand square meters creates an area in which everyone can make own discoveries. 

The Centre features the only Robotic Theatre in the world. The moves of its leading actors ¿ RoboThespians ¿ are controlled by compressed air, and their heartbeats are produced by a 40-Watt loudspeaker. 

In the CSC, everyone may feel like a real scientist bent over slides and test-tubes, surrounded by spectroscopes or electropneumatic sets. Our laboratories allow for independent experimenting. The physics, chemistry, biology and robotics labs are equipped with devices used in state-of-the-art laboratories all over the world. 

The building is surrounded with the Discovery Park. Its design was developed together by engineers, artists and greenery designers. Apart from art exhibits presenting sound effects, it also includes an open air gallery and a summer stage. 

The Centre co-organises the Science Picnic ¿ the largest open air event for the promotion of science on our continent. The commitment of scientists and interest of our audience have contributed to impressive achievements that we may be proud of in Europe. In 2005, the Science Picnic held in Warsaw was commended by the European Commission as one of ten model European projects in the "Science and Society" field. 

In June 2011, we opened one of the most modern planetaria in Europe. The Heavens of Copernicus makes it possible to watch over ten million stars. A spherical screen surrounds the auditorium from all sides, and the 3D technology makes the spectators feel immersed in the projected image. The planetarium is a venue of sky presentations, film shows, lectures and meetings. The Heavens of Copernicus Planetarium has its own production studio, where original film shows for our visitors are created. 

We are one of the youngest science centres, yet we are considered one of the most interesting and innovative centres in the world. The attendance rate in the Copernicus Science Centre proves the fundamental need to establish such institutions and bears witness to the considerable developmental ambitions of our society. Less than 2 years after the opening, we have been visited by over 2 million people.

The CSC is a cultural institution established and financed by the Capital City of Warsaw, the Ministry of Science and Higher Education and the Ministry of National Education.

The Centre features the only Robotic Theatre in the world. The moves of its leading actors ¿ RoboThespians ¿ are controlled by compressed air, and their heartbeats are produced by a 40-Watt loudspeaker. 

In the CSC, everyone may feel like a real scientist bent over slides and test-tubes, surrounded by spectroscopes or electropneumatic sets. Our laboratories allow for independent experimenting. The physics, chemistry, biology and robotics labs are equipped with devices used in state-of-the-art laboratories all over the world. 

The building is surrounded with the Discovery Park. Its design was developed together by engineers, artists and greenery designers. Apart from art exhibits presenting sound effects, it also includes an open air gallery and a summer stage. 

The Centre co-organises the Science Picnic ¿ the largest open air event for the promotion of science on our continent. The commitment of scientists and interest of our audience have contributed to impressive achievements that we may be proud of in Europe. In 2005, the Science Picnic held in Warsaw was commended by the European Commission as one of ten model European projects in the "Science and Society" field. 

In June 2011, we opened one of the most modern planetaria in Europe. The Heavens of Copernicus makes it possible to watch over ten million stars. A spherical screen surrounds the auditorium from all sides, and the 3D technology makes the spectators feel immersed in the projected image. The planetarium is a venue of sky presentations, film shows, lectures and meetings. The Heavens of Copernicus Planetarium has its own production studio, where original film shows for our visitors are created. 

We are one of the youngest science centres, yet we are considered one of the most interesting and innovative centres in the world. The attendance rate in the Copernicus Science Centre proves the fundamental need to establish such institutions and bears witness to the considerable developmental ambitions of our society. Less than 2 years after the opening, we have been visited by over 2 million people.

The CSC is a cultural institution established and financed by the Capital City of Warsaw, the Ministry of Science and Higher Education and the Ministry of National Education.

entityDescription: Fondazione CMCC is a non-profit research institution.CMCC’s mission is to investigate and model our climate system and its interactions with society to provide reliable, rigorous, and timely scientific results, which will in turn stimulate sustainable growth, protect the environment, and develop science driven adaptation and mitigation policies in a changing climate. CMCC collaborates with experienced scientists, economists, and technicians, which work together in order to provide full analyses of climate impacts on various systems such as agriculture, ecosystems, coasts, water resources, health, and economics.CMCC supports policymakers in setting and assessing costs, mitigation, and adaptation policies.It involves and links private and public institutions jointly investigating multidisciplinary topics related to climate science research. CMCC benefits from the extensive applied research experience of its members and institutional partners:Istituto Nazionale di Geofisica e Vulcanologia;Università del Salento;Università Ca’ Foscari Venezia; Università di Sassari; Università della Tuscia;Politecnico di Milano;Alma Mater Studiorum Università di Bologna: Resources for the Future. CMCC research activities are distributed among 3 Research Institutes, each of them grouping the CMCC Research Divisions: Institute for Earth System Predictions (IESP) it has the objective of promoting, organizing, and disseminating forecasts, simulations and scenarios of the Earth system at all scales IESP - Institute for the Forecasting of the Terrestrial System; it includes: ROFS - Regional Ocean Forecasting System;CLIVAP Climate Variability & prediction;ESYDA Earth System Modelling and Data Assimilation; ASC - Advanced Scientific Computing; GOCO - Global Coastal Ocean. Institute for Climate Resilience (ICR)it uses IESP products to develop new methodologies, provide information on risks and adaptation; it includes: IAFES Impacts on Agriculture, Forests and Ecosystem Services; RAAS-Risk Assessment and Adaptation Strategies; REMHI - REgional Models and geo-Hydrological Impacts; ISCD - Information Systems for Climate science and Decision-making.European Institute on Economics and the Environment (EIEE): it aims at supporting environmental, energy and natural resource decisions through economic research and interaction with national and international policies; it includes: Sustainable Earth Modelling Economics (SEME); Economic analysis of Climate Impacts and Policy (ECIP). CMCC acquired portfolio of research projects includes more than 600 funded projects:38 projects in FP6 and FP7, 84 projects in H2020, 73 in Horizon Europe & 420 projects under other EU and international research grants. CMCC Quality Management System is certified according to the ISO 9001:2008 standards (IQNet Certification No. 18049). Since 2008 CMCC operates its own Supercomputing Centre (SCC) located in Lecce at CMCC HQ.SCC is the only computational facility in Italy specializing in Climate Change research.

Johanniter-Unfall-Hilfe e.V. (Johanniter) is a German non-governmental organization dedicated to excellence in the fields of ambulance service, civil protection and disaster relief. With its more than
13,000 full-time and 22,000 voluntary staff, Johanniter is one of four organizations forming the backbone of the German ambulance and medical civil protection system.

Johanniter is active in the international arena with its branch of Johanniter International Assistance providing assistance in different areas and phases of disaster relief and humanitarian aid, with its core competences in the fields of primary health care, rehabilitation of people with disabilities and disaster preparedness. Johanniter International Assistance is present with field offices and/or cooperating with local partners e.g. in Haiti, Democratic Republic of Congo, Indonesia. Johanniter International Assistance is registered with DG ECHO concerning middle and long term projects as a Partner with status "p" within the Framework Partnership Agreement (FPA).

On the basis of the core competence in disaster preparedness, Johanniter has a long experience in
the international disaster relief environment and is actively involved in the EU Civil Protection
Mechanism: Since 2006, together with the partners, Cyprus Civil Defence (CCD), Bulgarian Chief Directorate for Fire Safety and Civil Protection and German Federal Agency for Technical Relief (THW), Johanniter conduct yet Assessment Mission Courses (AMC) for EU experts in Bulgaria/Cyprus, provides trainers and lecturers for various training courses contributes civil protection/disaster relief experts for missions and can support EUCP missions with its EUTAC TAST, e.g. in November/December 2010 due to the cholera outbreak in Haiti. Johanniter is a co-developer of the communication kits "EU Assessment Mission Kit" and "MIC in a Box" and has an agreement with the European Commission to maintain and provide these tools for EU missions. Furthermore, Johanniter was involved in the first year in the design, organization and conduct of EU module table-top exercises in Slovenia/Croatia.

Planning, managing, conducting and evaluating complex projects on an international level is part of
Johanniter's daily routine, in particular in the unit "International Projects and Cooperation" (IPC), under the auspices of Johanniter International Assistance in the national headquarters of Johanniter in Berlin. Johanniter is/was e.g. the coordinating beneficiary for the Preparatory Action projects EUTAC, EURAMET based on the calls for proposals for the Preparatory Action on an EU Rapid Response Capability of 2008 and 2009 and EURACARE, based on the call for proposals for Prevention and Preparedness 2011 under the Civil Protection Financial Instrument. EUTAC TAST, EURAMET and EURACARE, are registered modules in CECIS and available for EU CP interventions.

As integral part of the Johanniter Disaster Relief Concept, Johanniter has an International
Training Centre which organizes and coordinates trainings mainly of Johanniter volunteers to
train and prepare them for international missions. They cooperate for instance with the Federal Training
Centre of THW in Neuhausen a.d.F. or the Academy for Crisis Management, Emergency Planning and Civil Protection (AKNZ) in Bad Neuenahr-Ahrweiler.
